title: Occupant behaviour as a resource for acoustic comfort. Validation and evaluation of a device for the reduction of noise generated by occupants in classrooms and offices.
research_question: 1) To validate SEM device in densely occupied environments (primary school classrooms and open-plan offices); 2) To evaluate how occupants interact with SEM device and perceive external incentives (paper-based communication, researcher feedback, ICT-based solutions); 3) To identify a roadmap for the adoption of such a complete and qualified system in large-scale applications; 4) How do employees evaluate the effects of irrelevant speech noise on annoyance, performance, mental health and well-being, and occupant behaviour in shared and open-plan offices?; 5) Are there relationships between perceived noise annoyance, personal characteristics (age, gender, professional sector) and office characteristics (city, number of people, room acoustic design)?; 6) Which technical solutions can be applied for solving weaknesses and shortcomings of the Alpha prototype and existing devices, as well as for generating a scalable, accurate, adaptable and customizable prototype in view of the final implementation of the system?; 7) What is the accuracy of the Beta version of SEM prototype in measurement of reliable decibel levels in real environments compared to the 1-class Sound Level Meter?; 8) Does SEM device affect the background noise levels generated by pupils?; 9) Can independent variables (teacher, time-band, number of pupils, day of week, class) significantly affect the background noise levels in the two lighting feedback conditions?; 10) Can the motivational methods (constant feedback and/or game-based challenge) encourage pupils towards a long-term behavioural change?; 11) How do teachers assess the acoustic quality of classrooms? How do they perceive the presence of SEM device as an educational tool in classrooms also in relation to pupils’ behaviour?; 12) Do the teachers’ voice levels decrease when the lighting feedback of SEM devices is switched on in classrooms?; 13) Is there a significant difference in terms of voice levels and background noise levels when SEM devices are switched on, independently from the subjects?; 14) How does SEM device affect the vocal effort of each teacher and the background noise levels, class-by-class?; 15) How do teachers perceive their vocal status, noise condition and voice intensity with and without SEM devices?; 16) How do employees experience irrelevant speech in the investigated open-plan office?; 17) How and whether does irrelevant speech affect the annoyance, performance, mental health and well-being, occupant behaviour during the working hours?; 18) How do employees perceive the presence of SEM device on their desks during their working activities, as well as its functionality in terms of variation of lighting feedback?; 19) Are there technical issues related to the functionality of the Beta prototype of SEM device?

participants.description: Cross-sectional survey: 1078 employees (58% male, 42% female; 33% 26-35, 26% 36-50, 36% 51-65+ years old) from 19 companies, 5 research centers, 1 university in Italy (78% Turin). 55% in shared offices (2-5 occupants), 45% in open-plan offices (6-200 occupants). Classroom monitoring: 290 pupils (6-10 years old) and 25 teachers (38-60 years old, mean 48.4) from 13 primary school classes in Turin, Italy. Finnish open-plan office pilot: 10 employees from a university administration area in Turku, Finland.
participants.recruitment: Online questionnaire distributed via e-mail (cross-sectional survey); voluntary participation in long-term monitoring campaigns in schools and a pilot study in an open-plan office.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Shared offices (2-5 occupants) and open-plan offices (+5 occupants) in Italy.
Primary school classrooms in Turin, Italy, with varying acoustic conditions and teaching activities.
Finnish open-plan office (10.8 × 8.9 × 3.1 m) with 12 workstations, screens, and sound-absorbing materials.

SEM (Speech and Sound SEMaphore) device, Alpha prototype (totem with class 2 Sound Level Meter, LED lights) and Beta prototype (small table device with electret condenser microphone, microcontroller board, LED lights).
Lighting feedback (green, yellow, red colors) from SEM device, switched on or off.
Motivational methods: constant feedback (mobile app, whiteboard plots, reports) and/or game-based challenge.
Paper-based communication (visible reminder on color meaning, daily results) and web page for real-time/historical noise levels.
